messages.content: Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the payment to A in euros with one decimal place, from 0.0 to the offered rest; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the payment to A in euros with one decimal place, from 0.0 to the offered rest; no explanation.

After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Your game has no additional payment stage after acceptance. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the payment to A in euros with one decimal place, from 0.0 to the offered rest; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the payment to A in euros with one decimal place, from 0.0 to the offered rest; no explanation.

At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

Predict the observed choice of a human participant; do not solve for an optimal strategy. This is an anonymous two-person stochastic ultimatum game with fixed roles A (proposer) and B (responder). There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.

If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only the claim amount kept for A in euros, as a number with one decimal place, between 0.0 and 20.0; no explanation.

There are two phases of 10 rounds each. Within a phase the partner stays the same; phase 2 assigns a different anonymous partner. At each round a pie is drawn uniformly from 0.0 to 20.0 euros in 0.1-euro increments. A does not know the current pie when choosing a claim between 0.0 and 20.0 euros in 0.1 increments to keep for A. B then sees the pie, claim and rest=pie-claim and chooses accept or reject. If B rejects, both earn 0.0 euros that round. If B accepts, A earns the claim and B earns the rest; B may accept a negative rest, which incurs a loss, with a confirmation warning. In your game, only if B accepted and rest>0, B chooses a payment to A between 0.0 and rest in 0.1 increments; final round earnings are claim+payment for A and rest-payment for B. A zero payment is permitted. Every round ends with full feedback of the pie, decisions and both earnings; the phase ends with a full history. After phase 1 each participant writes a strategy reflection before rematching. One round from each phase is randomly selected for payment, plus a 5-euro endowment and earnings from a later separately instructed part; the final total cannot be negative. The content of the later part has not been disclosed during this main game. Prior feedback JSON uses euros; phase and round locate earlier feedback, claim_eur is A's claim, rest_eur=pie_eur-claim_eur, accepted is B's previous action, transfer_paid_eur is the realized payment (zero when none was made, not a claim that an extra decision occurred), and A_profit_eur/B_profit_eur are previous round earnings. Only the listed prior feedback has occurred. Do not treat the current decision's future consequences as known. Output only accept or reject; no explanation.
